nodes.label: environment-validation capability
nodes.rationale: Bootstrap D3: validate critical env vars (DATABASE_URI, PAYLOAD_SECRET) with Zod in a server-only module (src/lib/env/) invoked by both payload.config.ts and Next.js server startup, so a missing/invalid value fails explicitly at boot/build rather than later at runtime; rejected validating only inside route handlers as insufficient. Payload-cms-core D9 later modifies this: Payload's CLI (generate:types, migrate:create) loads payload.config.ts outside the Next.js bundler via a stricter loader that cannot load a module guarded by 'server-only', cannot resolve the tsconfig '@/*' alias, and chokes on richtext-lexical's top-level await. Fix: a second minimal module src/lib/env/payload.ts (no server-only guard, validates only DATABASE_URI/PAYLOAD_SECRET) used exclusively by payload.config.ts, while src/lib/env/index.ts keeps its server-only guard for the rest of the app; rejected removing the server-only guard entirely because it would weaken protection against accidental client-bundle inclusion.

nodes.rationale: Separates the CMS schema for a block (manual vs automatic selection) from the rendered UI Section, so a Section never needs to know whether its data came from manual or automatic content selection; unknown blocks log and skip instead of crashing the page.

nodes.label: Tag-based cache and targeted revalidation
nodes.rationale: Using conceptual cache tags (post:{id}, category:{id}, home, navigation, footer, settings) instead of full rebuilds lets publish/update operations invalidate only the dependent content, while Draft Mode must never serve stale public cache to a previewing editor.

nodes.label: Data Access Layer (src/lib/data)
nodes.rationale: Centralizing Payload queries in one layer (getPostBySlug, getLatestPosts, searchPosts, etc.) keeps presentational components query-free and allows the backend to be swapped without touching UI components.

nodes.label: Payload/Next.js separation of responsibilities
nodes.rationale: Payload decides what content exists and its order; Next.js decides how it looks. This split keeps the CMS from emitting arbitrary CSS/HTML/scripts and keeps presentation logic out of the CMS, preventing an uncontrolled visual builder and preserving a consistent editorial design system.

nodes.label: React Server Components by default
nodes.rationale: Minimizes client-side JavaScript and supports progressive enhancement; only components with a genuine browser need (mobile nav, share actions, carousels, accordions) become Client Components.

nodes.label: Source-of-truth conflict priority order
nodes.rationale: Establishes a deterministic precedence (Master Spec > active OpenSpec change > existing verified implementation > tool/skill guidance > agent judgment) so that when instructions conflict, agents resolve deterministically instead of guessing or introducing a third architecture.

nodes.label: Editorial Components (capability)
nodes.rationale: Provides the presentational, data-free editorial component set as reusable foundation for later-phase pages.

nodes.label: Presentational-only Component Pattern
nodes.rationale: No editorial component may query Payload directly (Local API, REST/GraphQL, or DB); all data arrives via props, keeping components reusable and testable independent of the CMS.

nodes.label: local-docker-environment capability

D8: node_modules lives in its own container volume, never overwritten by the host's node_modules, so macOS-compiled native binaries don't replace the Linux ones the container needs.

nodes.label: cms-access-control capability
nodes.rationale: D1: Posts/Pages access.read returns true for authenticated users and restricts anonymous requests to _status:published; Posts additionally declares create/update:isAdminOrWriter and delete:isAdmin after task-16.3 live verification found that Payload defaults any undefined access operation to () => true, which had briefly left Posts create/update/delete open to unauthenticated requests — the other 6 collections already defined their full access block. D2: Users keeps collection-level read open but hides email/role/active via field-level access so the public author shape (displayName/slug/avatar/bio/socialLinks) stays readable without exposing sensitive fields; rejected access.read:()=>false at the collection level. D3: a minimal beforeLogin hook blocks session tokens for active:false accounts, deliberately narrow so it doesn't touch other lifecycle behavior reserved for Phase 3.

nodes.rationale: D11: Media.mimeTypes excludes image/svg+xml in this phase because SVG can carry active content and no sanitization mechanism exists yet; deferred to a later phase alongside sanitization.
